Turron de Alicante (Hard Almond Nougat)

Served at: Immaculada

One 8x4 inch (20x10 cm) bar, about 12 servingsPrep 25 minCook 30 min

Turron de Alicante is a classic Spanish hard nougat, a beloved confection especially popular during the Christmas season. Its appearance on tables for the Feast of the Immaculate Conception (Immaculada) on December 8th often signals the official start of holiday festivities in Spain, bringing families together to share this sweet, crunchy treat.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (200g) blanched whole almonds
  • 1/2 cup (170g) honey
  • 1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar
  • 2 tablespoons (30ml) water
  • 1 large egg white
  • Pinch of salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon lemon zest (optional)
  • 2 sheets edible wafer paper (oblea), approximately 8x4 inches (20x10 cm) each

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C). Spread the blanched almonds in a single layer on a baking sheet and toast for 10-15 minutes, or until lightly golden and fragrant. Let them cool completely.
  2. Line an 8x4 inch (20x10 cm) loaf pan or a similar-sized mold with parchment paper, leaving an overhang on the sides. Place one sheet of wafer paper on the bottom of the mold.
  3. In a small, heavy-bottomed saucepan, combine the honey. Heat it over medium-low heat until it reaches 250°F (121°C) on a candy thermometer. Remove from heat immediately.
  4. In another small, heavy-bottomed saucepan, combine the granulated sugar and water. Heat over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Once dissolved, stop stirring and let it boil until it reaches 290°F (143°C) on a candy thermometer (hard crack stage). Remove from heat.
  5. While the syrups are heating, in a clean, dry bowl, beat the egg white with a pinch of salt using an electric mixer on medium-high speed until stiff peaks form.
  6. With the mixer running on low speed, slowly and carefully drizzle the hot honey into the egg white mixture. Increase speed to medium-high and beat for 2-3 minutes until well combined.
  7. Reduce the mixer speed to low again and slowly and carefully drizzle the hot sugar syrup into the egg white mixture. Increase speed to medium-high and continue beating for about 5-7 minutes, or until the mixture is very thick, glossy, and holds its shape.
  8. Gently fold in the toasted almonds and lemon zest (if using) into the nougat mixture with a sturdy spatula until evenly distributed.
  9. Quickly transfer the mixture into the prepared mold, spreading it evenly. Place the second sheet of wafer paper on top and press down gently.
  10. Place another piece of parchment paper on top, followed by a heavy, flat object (like a cutting board with cans on top) to press the turron down firmly. Let it cool completely at room temperature for at least 6-8 hours, or preferably overnight.
  11. Once fully set, remove the turron from the mold using the parchment paper overhang. Carefully peel off the parchment paper and cut the turron into desired pieces using a sharp, heavy knife.
  12. Serve at room temperature and enjoy the festive flavors.

Tips

  • A candy thermometer is essential for success; precise temperatures are key for the nougat's texture.
  • Work quickly once the almonds are folded in, as the mixture will begin to set.
  • Store turron in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2-3 weeks, separating layers with parchment paper if stacking.
